data.turoyo: Omər: "Abri, dowe ḥa lḥuḏe w ʕaṣro w ʕəsri w mo w maṯe, luno w luxat lə kmakfən. Qay gzayʕət?"
data.translation: Der Vater sprach: "Mein Sohn! Ob es einer ist oder zehn oder zwanzig oder zweihundert, gegen mich und dich können sie doch nicht aufkommen. Warum fürchtest du dich?"

rationale: Fill Infectum 1 from three to four; competitive-strength comparison with l-persons is a useful contrast to ordinary resource sufficiency.

data.turoyo: Səmli zuwade, d makəfyo l šabṯo! W lo koṯeno, hul d lo ṣoyadno i ġazalayo."
data.translation: Mach mir mal Wegzehrung für eine Woche zurecht! Ich komme nicht wieder, bis ich nicht die Gazelle erjagt habe.

rationale: Fill Infectum 1 to five; provisions as resource, l-šabṯo duration as standard, rather than a personal beneficiary.

summary: All 25 occurrences express sufficiency, including absolute enough in payment/refusal and discourse closure. Resources range over money, food, ovens, animals, grazing land and armed groups; none requires a transitive make-enough sense.

The sufficient resource is the subject and agrees in number/gender; persons for whom it suffices are l-marked or suffix-coded, sometimes doubled by an independent pronoun. l- also marks a temporal measure (52/106;115/210). These clauses do not show ordinary direct-object coding.

The salary dialogue 70/193 contrasts Komakfəlluxne and lə kmakfəlline with the same plural resource. The suffix sequence resembles already quoted Gmakfəllaxne (64/32), so it is not an unattested form.
Only one Infectum-wa occurrence is supplied and it is already quoted at 2/40. Do not duplicate it. Existing Infectum count is three; the two selected contexts bring it to five.

58/95 supplied kmafyoliyo differs from the editors’ k-makfiyó-li-yo. This is an unresolved textual/dialectal discrepancy, not license to silently overwrite either witness or add the same citation twice.
Does the missing k in supplied kmafyoliyo (58/95) reflect sound reduction, a transcription error, or another source layer? Verify against the edition/recording before changing the existing form.
Confirm final -ne segmentation in Gmakfəllaxne, Komakfəlluxne and gmakfəlline, and its relationship to singular -yo. Are these agreeing resumptive elements or part of the suffix complex?
Do speakers recognize the hostile l-opponent use as an independent conventional sense, or as ordinary sufficiency evaluated against an opponent? Current evidence supports the latter.
How is the feminine/resource agreement in Haṯe k̬makfo (MAC NE Interview 2/68) construed: the performance, its amount, or an omitted feminine noun?
Hostile groups may fail to suffice against a person or group (29/359;113/214), yielding “not be a match for”. Retain sufficiency sense 1 rather than make a second sense solely for opponents.
